what: Provenance for every ledger under bench/phase0-agent-native/ that stamps a measuredCommit. Those stamps name PRE-SQUASH BRANCH commits: this repository squash-merges, so the squash discards them and no third party can resolve them — three of five are contained by zero remote branches and survive only as unreferenced objects in individual clones. Every roadmap since 0.15 cites them as the provenance of its published numbers.
publicationStampsWhat: #1417: the website's benchmark data (website/public/data/*.json) stamps SHORT commits (c2a8816d, 107462e, 580e189). Those stamps stay exactly as published — they are historical records, and the inventory classifies the files stale (#1276, #1422). publicationStamps records, beside each one, the full commit its prefix uniquely expands to on main, with that commit's trees and manifest hashes. It identifies a commit; it does not make the published numbers valid.
history: schemaVersion 1 (#1199) recorded resolvableOnMain and asserted each basis without verifying it, and checked reachability from HEAD. schemaVersion 2 (#1417) keeps every #1199 field unchanged and adds durableIdentity beside it; resolvableOnMain must equal durableIdentity.commit. No measuredCommit was changed.
whyNotJustRepointTheStamps: Because measuredCommit is the experimental record, not a pointer. Repointing it would falsify what was measured, and effect-rows-benefit-ledger.json's stamp is additionally ARM_B_COMMIT — a frozen constant of a completed epoch, pinned by ppw-compile.py, ppw-analyze.py and PpWRowsRegistrationTests. Two of these ledgers are also byte-compared against their own generators, so a field added by hand would make them permanently 'stale'. The stamps stay; this file carries the resolvable equivalent beside them.

basisKinds.identical-src-tree: STRONGEST. A commit reachable from main whose `src/` tree is byte-identical to the measured commit's, verified with `git rev-parse <sha>:src` on both. Same compiler; a third party can check the numbers against it.
basisKinds.landing-commit-only: WEAKER, and said so. No commit reachable from main has an identical `src/` tree, so the exact compiler state was never landed as such. The commit named is the squash that carried the LEDGER onto main — where the numbers landed, not the compiler that produced them.
basisKinds.measured-on-top-of: The numbers were measured with the landing change APPLIED to the named commit, which is what regenerating a ledger inside the PR that moves it always means. The stamp its generator writes is HEAD at regeneration time, and the squash commit that will carry the change does not exist yet — the #1159 bootstrapping problem, and the reason this index exists rather than a rule that the stamp must equal the landing commit.
basisKinds.unique-prefix-expansion: For a historical SHORT stamp (#1417). The stamp stays as written; the durable commit is the only object in a full clone whose id starts with it, verified with `git rev-parse --disambiguate`. It names a commit on main; it cannot show the files were produced from a clean checkout of that commit. Short stamps can collide (see effect-rows-benefit-ledger.json), which is why the expansion is re-checked for uniqueness rather than trusted.
basisKinds.post-merge-write-back: Contract v0.24 §6(b), for a measurement whose final squash commit cannot exist before merge. Phase 1 (in the PR): durableIdentity {status: pending, phase1 {headCommit = the measuredCommit, pr, treeHashes, inputContentHashes, artifactSha256}}. phase1.treeHashes must claim src (the measured compiler), never "/"; the entry carries no resolvableOnMain. A pending identity is NEVER authoritative. Phase 2 (a write-back PR after merge): the commit on protected main that landed the artifact, with every phase-1 tree re-verified equal there; the phase-1 record is kept under writeBack and must equal the pending entry committed in this index AT the landing commit (so it cannot be rewritten later); every phase-1 tree and manifest is re-checked there on every run; the durable commit must be the one that landed the artifact, and the committed artifact must still be those bytes. If any tree or manifest differs the write-back fails and the numbers must be re-measured.

identity.shape: durableIdentity {status, commit, resolvedVia, treeHashes, inputContentHashes}. measuredCommit is the historical stamp and never changes; the durable identity is recorded beside it.
identity.commit: Full 40-hex SHA that is an ancestor of fetched refs/remotes/origin/main (resolvedVia). HEAD, refs/pull/N/merge, branches, short SHAs, and tags are rejected. §6 also allows an immutable release tag; this repository's v* tags are lightweight and unprotected, so none qualifies and the stricter rule applies.
identity.treeHashes: Repository path -> git object id at commit (`git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`); "/" is the whole repository tree (`<commit>^{tree}`) and is required, so every repository-resident input (corpus gitlinks, fixtures, configuration) is covered, not only src. Re-read and compared on every run.
identity.inputContentHashes: Repository path -> SHA-256 of the manifest bytes at commit (`git cat-file blob <commit>:<path>`).
identity.measuredTreeHashes: identical-src-tree only: the trees claimed identical, verified at BOTH measuredCommit and the durable commit.
identity.clone: Validation fails, never skips, in a shallow clone or one without refs/remotes/origin/main.
identity.writeBackCommand: CALOR_PROVENANCE_WRITEBACK=1 dotnet test tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~LedgerCommitStampTests.PendingIdentities" (after `git fetch origin main`); commit the rewritten index in a write-back PR.
identity.landing: measured-on-top-of only: the commit that landed the artifact (holds its current bytes, its first parent does not), on main and descending from the stamped base, with its src tree.

ledgers.note: #1677 originally regenerated at 655bd907: removing duplicate receiver/argument conversions reduced Calor0411 sites to MediatR 289, serilog 722 and FluentValidation 5766. #1588/#1686 continuation remeasured at 4e87980e, including restored metadata-string null patterns, exact query-continuation receiver typing, and the integrated website/oracle heads, with the automatic pinned-CLI cross-check: Calor0425 143 -> 142 sites, still 52 diagnostic modules of 276 enforced; Calor0411 sites serilog 722 -> 695 and FluentValidation 5766 -> 4486, MediatR unchanged. Explicit preservation of unsupported ordered operands, patterns, constructor labels and collection targets reduces native coverage; these falls are not binding or effect-resolution improvements. All 364 selected outputs still parse. The phase-1 identity was pending until the post-merge write-back; the completed identity resolves to protected-main landing c9105a726 with all measured inputs unchanged. Earlier identities remain in repository history.

#901/#1590 (0.29, PR #1721): regenerated both demand legs at 76270627d after runtime PE-metadata reuse and deterministic verification-context ownership, with CALOR_REGENERATE_HIGHER_ORDER_DEMAND_LEDGER=1. Corpus inputs and measured counts are unchanged from finalized native SQL: 52 pre-effect failures and demandTotal 3123. The previous measurement and completed identity remain in git history. Pending phase 1 is not an authoritative protected-main identity.

#901/#1590 (0.29, PR #1721): regenerated at 76270627d after runtime PE-metadata reuse and deterministic verification-context ownership, with CALOR_REGENERATE_EFFECT_RESOLVER_KEY_LEDGER=1. Corpus inputs and counts are unchanged from finalized native SQL: aggregate 283 bound / 880 string keys, including seven benchmark files with 18 bound / 53 string keys. Floors are unchanged. The previous measurement and completed identity remain in git history. Pending phase 1 is not an authoritative protected-main identity.

The measured commit is not present in this clone at all, so no tree comparison is possible. It is also ARM_B_COMMIT and must not move. Worth recording: it shares its first EIGHT hex characters with main's real v0.15.0 release commit 3bb2601e3ff83597ddf2f27dcc334b6399ab97ea, which is why short shas looked right to every reader until now.
